new_findings.summary: Section 3.2.1 states the replay-vs-mirror finding-authority invariant only for the 'Codex-Korrekturauftrag', and Slice 1 Arbeitsschritt 4 repeats 'vor dem Aufbau eines nativen Codex-Korrekturauftrags'. In the current code (workflow.py _run_codex, lines ~1493-1535), CODEX_PLAN_REVISION is dispatched under NativeCodexRequestKind.PLAN, not NativeCodexRequestKind.CORRECTION, which is reserved for CODEX_CORRECTION/CODEX_FINAL_CORRECTION. A literal reading of 3.2.1/Arbeitsschritt 4 could therefore be implemented as applying the mirror-vs-replay integrity check only to CORRECTION-kind requests, silently exempting plan-revision requests even though 3.3.5 asserts all three variants share one finding lifecycle. Confirmed against the repository: history.findings, which feeds _native_codex_request, is currently populated by orchestrator.py:_history() from state.runtime_history (the state-v3 mirror), not from a record-chain replay -- so today there is no replay-derived authority check on any Codex request path, and the plan must bind the new check to all Codex-bearing request kinds explicitly, including the PLAN kind used for revisions.

acceptance_test.text: Before Slice 1 is marked complete, produce a test that starts a run with an open Claude finding, forces state.runtime_history (mirror) and the persisted FindingTransitionPayload chain to diverge, and asserts that BOTH a CODEX_PLAN_REVISION request build (NativeCodexRequestKind.PLAN) and a CODEX_CORRECTION request build (NativeCodexRequestKind.CORRECTION) stop fail-closed before any provider invocation, using the replayed record chain as the sole authority in each case.

new_findings.summary: Section 3.3.2 proposes adding an optional finding_dispositions field to plan_result inside schemas/native-agent-codex-result-v1.schema.json while keeping schema_version as the same const value ('native-agent-codex-result-v1'). The module that consumes this schema (src/native_codex_contract.py) is explicitly documented as 'Closed native Codex JSON results'. The plan correctly reserves a fallback to an explicit v2 decision if this creates 'semantic ambiguity', per Section 7's stop conditions, but gives no concrete criterion for what constitutes that ambiguity, leaving the actual go/no-go judgment to implementation time with no falsifiable test defined in the plan itself.

acceptance_test.text: Before patching the schema, Slice 1 records in the plan/PR description: (a) a re-validation of every fixture and any historical plan_result documents against the patched schema showing zero validation-outcome change, (b) confirmation that no code path treats schema_version=native-agent-codex-result-v1 as an exhaustive field-set marker (only as a discriminator), and (c) that 'dispositions required when open findings exist' is enforced in the domain layer (native_codex_contract.py / workflow.py), not via a schema 'required' change that would reject historically-valid documents. If any of the three cannot be shown, implementation stops and introduces schema_version=native-agent-codex-result-v2 instead of mutating the v1 constant's shape.

review_evidence.dimensions: Verified against repository state at base commit 0448788: (1) contract closure -- schemas/native-agent-codex-result-v1.schema.json plan_result currently has no finding_dispositions field (additionalProperties:false), confirming the plan's stated Vertrags-Gap is real; (2) backward compatibility -- plan's 'historical plan_result without the field reads as empty sequence' approach is schema-additive and testable; (3) reviewer-owned finding authority -- src/artifact_models.py FindingTransitionPayload.__post_init__ already enforces 'only the reporting reviewer may mutate a finding' and 'only codex may record a finding response' with finding_status forced to stay open on a codex response, matching 3.2.4/3.2.6 without new record types; (4) record/state precedence -- orchestrator.py:_history() currently derives WorkflowHistory.findings from state.runtime_history (state-v3 mirror), not from record-chain replay, confirming the plan's own repository-Befund and validating that Slice 1 Arbeitsschritt 4 is necessary new work, not already-solved; a precedent pattern for pure record-chain finding derivation already exists in final_review_preflight.py (latest_findings built by scanning FindingTransitionPayload records) that Slice 1 can reuse; (5) request/fingerprint binding -- native_codex_request.py already threads open_findings from previous_findings into every native Codex request regardless of kind, so the transport plumbing pre-exists and only the plan_result response side and the mirror-vs-replay authority check are missing; (6) exact-once/crash recovery -- orchestrator.py already exposes recover_pending_native_codex and recover_pending_native_reviewer with record-ahead raw-response persistence for both roles individually, supporting the plan's claim that Slice 2 only needs to chain and fault-inject existing mechanisms rather than invent new ones; (7) legacy isolation -- docs/internal/native-agent-json-manueller-bootstrap.md explicitly states it does not use run_task/--watch and does not replace the regular State-v3 production contract, and workflow.py's run_current_work_unit loop still contains unmodified ANTIGRAVITY_* steps, confirming the Antigravity-boundary stop in this plan does not weaken the production three-reviewer approval contract; (8) scope completeness against docs/internal/ORCHESTRATOR_ROADMAP_PHASE_2_PLUS.md Arbeitspaket 5 bullet list -- plan's invariants (3.1-3.5) and non-goals (Section 7) map 1:1 to the roadmap bullets, including the explicit no-new-record-type and no-direct-agent-communication constraints; (9) slice independence -- Slice 1 and Slice 2 are explicitly sequential (Section 6: Slice 2 begins only after Slice 1's own Claude review), each with a distinct, non-overlapping acceptance-criteria set and its own test files, which is the intended granularity for this roadmap's per-package slicing rather than parallel independence.
review_evidence.largest_residual_risk: The single most consequential open risk is that the mirror-vs-replay finding-authority check (3.2.1) is textually anchored to 'Codex-Korrekturauftrag' while the code's own NativeCodexRequestKind enum routes CODEX_PLAN_REVISION through the PLAN kind, not CORRECTION -- an implementer following the literal wording could wire the fail-closed replay check only into the CORRECTION path and leave CODEX_PLAN_REVISION trusting the state-v3 mirror, which is exactly the authority-precedence violation this whole work package exists to close, and it would surface only under a mirror/record divergence that is otherwise rare in normal operation.
review_evidence.break_condition: This approval breaks if Slice 1 ships with the replay-vs-mirror authority check implemented for CODEX_CORRECTION/CODEX_FINAL_CORRECTION only and CODEX_PLAN_REVISION continues to read history.findings straight from the state.runtime_history mirror without a fail-closed divergence check, or if the plan_result schema patch causes any previously-valid persisted plan_result document to fail validation, or if finding_dispositions is added as a required (not optional) field for plan_result in a way that breaks historical reads.

pre_mortem: If this plan fails in practice, the most likely path is: Slice 1 patches plan_result and wires the replay-derived finding check into the literal 'correction' code path (CODEX_CORRECTION/CODEX_FINAL_CORRECTION) while CODEX_PLAN_REVISION, still classified as NativeCodexRequestKind.PLAN, keeps consuming history.findings from the state-v3 mirror unchanged. Tests pass because Slice 1's and Slice 2's scenario lists (Section 5, items 1-6) don't include an explicit state-mirror-vs-record-chain divergence case specifically for plan revision (item 14 mentions 'State-Mirror hinter oder vor der autoritativen Recordkette' generically but the Slice 1/2 test file lists don't force it onto the PLAN-kind path specifically). Months later, a resumed run after a partial persistence failure ends up with a stale mirror that still shows an already-closed Claude finding as open (or vice versa); a CODEX_PLAN_REVISION request is built from that stale mirror, Codex answers a finding that no longer reflects the authoritative record chain, and the resulting native plan_result silently diverges from the append-only truth -- exactly the reviewer-authority violation the whole package was meant to prevent, but only reachable through the one gap this review flags as C-01. The schema-versioning ambiguity (C-02) is a slower-burning risk: without a concrete disambiguation test, a rushed implementation could patch the 'closed' v1 schema in a way that a downstream tool pinning schema_version=native-agent-codex-result-v1 as an exhaustive contract silently starts seeing an unexpected optional field, which would only be caught by an unrelated integration much later.
